question: Which OSIRIS-REx source shows particle ejections at Bennu on 6 and 19 January 2019?

search.channel: Targeted public web search, followed by inspection of the sources listed below
search.query: NASA Bennu observed episodic ejection particles Lauretta 2019 Chesley mechanism meteoroid thermal fracture paper Bennu particle ejection model 2020
search.coverage: Three selected reports from one query. Database hit totals, exhaustive retrieval and independent double screening were outside this exercise.

criterion: Include an original research report after checking image-based evidence for the two specified events. Exclude public retellings from the evidence count. Defer a follow-up when its event coverage or observation overlap still needs checking.

claim.text: OSIRIS-REx navigation images recorded discrete particle ejections at Bennu on 6 and 19 January 2019.
claim.scope: The two selected events and the images and motion analysis in the original report. Physical causes and event frequency remain outside this claim.

reports.title: Episodes of particle ejection from the surface of the active asteroid (101955) Bennu
reports.position: Article p. 2 of 10, Fig. 1 panels A-D and caption, and the paragraphs describing the two NavCam image pairs and particle motion.
reports.reason: The research team presents its images for both selected dates and explains how the image pairs distinguish moving particles.

relation.rationale: The January 6 and 19 sequences each contain particles whose positions shift relative to the asteroid. The paper associates their motion with discrete ejection events.
relation.scope: Two events imaged by the same mission. Other dates, detection completeness and a unique physical cause require separate evidence.

reports.title: NASA’s OSIRIS-REx Mission Explains Bennu’s Mysterious Particle Events
reports.position: Opening image caption and paragraph referring to the team's December 6 Science paper.
reports.reason: The mission news article summarizes the same observations as the included paper. Counting it again would duplicate those observations.

reports.title: Trajectory Estimation for Particles Observed in the Vicinity of (101955) Bennu
reports.version: Chesley et al., Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets (2020)
reports.position: Abstract and Introduction paragraphs describing the extension of the 2019 analysis, the observation window and selection effects.
reports.reason: The follow-up covers a wider time span and builds on the first paper. Matching its trajectory data to individual January images remains open, so this pass assigns no additional evidence for the two events.
